english.title: Make funds available for benefit of designated person - Ukraine
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without authority of a licence granted by the Treasury, made funds available, namely, **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF FUNDS..) to any person, namely **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF PERSON..), for the benefit of a designated person, namely **(..SPECIFY DESIGNATED PERSON..), knowing or having reasonable cause to suspect that you were making the funds so available
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 5(1) , 10(1) and 12(1) of the Ukraine (European Union Financial Sanctions) (No.2) Regulations 2014.

english.notes:
(i) A designated person means a person, entity or body listed in Annex I to the Council Regulation.
(ii) Funds are made available for the benefit of a designated person only if that person obtains or is able to obtain a significant financial benefit.
(iii) Frozen account means an account with a relevant institution which is held or controlled (directly or indirectly) by a designated person.
(iv) Regulation 8 states that the offence outlined by regulation 4 will not be committed when a person /relevant institution credits a frozen account with:(a) interest or other earning due on the account;
(b) payments due under contracts / agreements / obligations that arose before the account was frozen;
(c) payments due under judicial, administrative / arbitral decisions rendered or enforceable by a Member State. (v) A relevant institution must inform the Treasury without delay if they credit a frozen account in line with paragraphs (1)(b), (c) or paragraph 2 of regulation 8.
(vi) The offence does not apply to anything done under the authority of a licence granted by the Treasury. If a licence is varied / revoked by the Treasury, an offence may still be made out as per regulation 9.
(vii) This offence may be committed by conduct wholly or partly outside the United Kingdom when it is the conduct of a UK national or a body incorporated or constituted under the law of the United Kingdom.
(viii) For provisions regarding the laying of proceedings, see regulation 13 for full detail of how proceedings may be brought in the relevant jurisdiction.
(ix) Regulation 14 states that consent of the Attorney General is needed to bring proceedings for this offence, except for summary offences.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 7 years imprisonment and/or fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
In relation to an offence committed before section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes in to force, the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
